IFR reports 2025 robot density led by South Korea at 1,066 per 10,000 workers

On November 12, IFR reported 1,066 operating industrial robots per 10,000 manufacturing employees in South Korea, followed by Singapore at 873 and Germany at 469. The global average is 152. This measures robots relative to employment, not annual new installations.

International Federation of Robotics ↗12 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

The latest density figures

On November 12, IFR reported 1,066 operating industrial robots per 10,000 manufacturing employees in South Korea, followed by Singapore at 873 and Germany at 469. The global average is 152. This measures robots relative to employment, not annual new installations.

Regional comparisons

EU-27 density reached 240, up about 35% between 2020 and 2025. North America reached 214, up around 24%, and Asia 144, up around 47%. Japan ranks fourth at 452 and the United States eighth at 323.

The denominator matters

IFR places China at 193 and nineteenth globally using National Economic Census employment data. Workforce definitions must therefore be considered alongside robot counts. Density helps compare differently sized economies but does not directly measure productivity, job quality or individual factory-project success.
